exercise1.hint: Three print statements, one under the other. Python runs them top to bottom, and that order is the whole point of the exercise.

choices: The speed at which code runs
The order in which statements are executed
How much memory a program uses
questions.explain: By default Python runs top to bottom. Conditionals and loops are how you change that order.

questions.prompt: Without any conditionals or loops, how does a Python script run?
questions.explain: Straight-line execution is the default; everything else in this unit is a way of departing from it.

questions.prompt: Which of these changes control flow?
questions.explain: An if statement lets a block run or not run, which is exactly what changing the flow means.
